title: GPMC's OS picker expands one family choice into an eleven-predicate edition union

provenance.note: Anchored to the same genuine WS2025 GPMC capture as server-10x-collision; the eleven predicates below are transcribed verbatim from the capture, which mixes server-family (WINTHRESHOLDSRV) and client-family (WINTHRESHOLD) tokens.

predicate.operator_goal: One OS-family choice in the GPMC picker (recent Windows family)

derivations: One picker choice becomes an OR over edition/service-pack tokens: GPMC enumerates the editions the family choice covers rather than emitting one wildcard predicate.

The union mixes WINTHRESHOLDSRV (server family) with WINTHRESHOLD (client family) entries and includes legacy edition codes (64STGSTD, 64MPPREM, 64ESSSOL) that no current OS reports; a reader must not 'clean up' predicates it considers dead.
Predicates carrying edition=NE or type=NE ('not evaluated') are part of the genuine emission and must round-trip verbatim.

Studio's ILT model must preserve this union exactly on import (no collapse, no deduplication, no reordering assumptions beyond XML order) and any future writer that offers a family picker must emit the same expansion to be GPMC-identical.

open_questions: Is this exact union stable across GPMC versions, or does the WS2025 picker add/remove edition tokens relative to older captures? A comparison capture from an older GPMC would settle it; none exists in the corpus yet.
